author: ohtadmin
title: Felix A. Porcaro
text:
It’s with deep sorrow that we announce the death of Felix A. Porcaro, Jr., 70, of Jamestown, R.I., and Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., who passed away peacefully Feb. 28, 2026, after a life full of love, laughter and happiness.
A devoted husband, beloved father and grandfather, visionary entrepreneur and generous philanthropist, Felix left an indelible mark on the jewelry industry and on the community he loved.
Felix was the beloved husband of Lori (DeSano) Porcaro for 47 years, sharing a marriage filled with love, laughter and devotion to family. Born in Providence, he was the son of the late Felix A. Porcaro, Sr. and Marie (Fera) Porcaro.
A proud alumnus of La Salle Academy, Felix remained deeply committed to his alma mater, earning induction into its Alumni Hall of Fame in 2014. He later served on the Board of Directors and established a family endowment to support students.
Felix’s professional influence spanned more than five decades. His career began at Femic, Inc., transforming it into AAi Foster Grant. Following this success, he founded Crimzon Rose International, becoming a major force in jewelry distribution.
In 2014, he acquired Uncas International, known for its licensed products featured in major theme parks around the world. In the last seven years of his career, Felix poured his creativity and passion into his work, serving as a visionary leader enthusiastic about the work he loved.
Felix’s accomplishments earned widespread recognition. In 2012, he received the Fashion Accessories Achievement Award and was named Man of the Year by the Italo American Club of Rhode Island.
Guided by their faith and commitment to serving others, Felix and Lori, along with Father Edward Cardente, founded the St. Edward Food and Wellness Center, a cornerstone of the Providence community, supporting thousands of families through food assistance and essential services. His dedication to improving the lives of children also led to the creation of the Botvin, Porcaro, Teverow Therapeutic Playground, an innovative therapeutic and educational resource for young children in Providence.
Felix lived by one of his favorite quotes from John Lennon: “A dream you dream alone is only a dream. A dream you dream together is reality.” He believed deeply in collaboration, family, and community — and he built a life that reflected those values every day.
He is survived by his beloved wife, Lori Porcaro; his children, Felice Silvia and her husband David, Felix Porcaro III and his wife Jennifer, and David Porcaro and his wife Ana. He leaves behind his treasured grandchildren, Arthur and Andrew Silvia; Felix IV, London and Scarlett Porcaro; Nicholas, Joseph and John Tsonos. He also is survived by his siblings, Linda Cerce, Beverly Casinelli, and Vincent Porcaro; as well as his cousin, who was like a brother to him, Arthur “Squeaky” Porcaro. He also leaves behind many loving nieces, nephews, dear friends and respected business associates.
He was predeceased by his brother, Patrick Porcaro, and his brothers-in-law, Gerald Cerce and Steven Casinelli.
Visiting hours will be from 4-7 p.m. Friday, March 6, 2026, at A. A. Mariani & Son Funeral Home, 200 Hawkins St., Providence.
A Mass of Christian Burial will be celebrated at 11 a.m. Saturday, March 7, 2026, at St. Ann Church, 280 Hawkins St., Providence. Burial will continue in St. Mark Cemetery, East Shore Road, Jamestown.
If street parking is unavailable, guests attending Mass are welcome to park in the A. A. Mariani & Son Funeral Home parking lot and walk to St. Ann Church.
Flowers are respectfully omitted. In lieu of flowers, memorial donations in Felix’s name may be made to the St. Edward Food and Wellness Center, 1001 Branch Ave., Providence, RI 02904, or by visiting www.stedwardfoodcenter.org.
Felix’s enduring spirit, generosity, and leadership are lasting gifts to all who knew him. His light will continue to shine in the hearts of his family and friends, and his legacy will resonate for generations to come.
Additional information at www.marianiandson.com.
